title: Build Nevada Table from Shipment and Repair Warranty Data
navigation: Build Nevada Table from Warranty Data
labelShipNote: SHIPMENT dataset: set as the ACTIVE dataset before opening this dialog. Select your production date and delivered columns below.
labelRepairNote: REPAIR dataset: select from the dropdown below. Once selected its columns will appear for mapping.
shipProdMonthCol: Shipment: Select the Production date column
shipDeliveredCol: Shipment: Select the Delivered / units shipped column
labelRepairCols: Repair dataset columns (available after selecting repair dataset above)
repairProdMonthCol: Repair: Select the Production date column
repairMonthCol: Repair: Select the Repair / failure date column
chkPreAggregated: Repair data is pre-aggregated (one row per production date / repair date combination, with a count column)
repairCountCol: Repair: Select the repair count column (number of repairs per row)
labelPreAggNote: When checked, the module sums the count column instead of counting rows. Leave unchecked if each row represents a single repair event (transactional format).
subPeriodCutoffs: Sub-period cut-off values (comma-separated, same format as Production Period). Leave blank to generate a single Nevada table. With N sub-periods, enter N cut-off values -- each is the FIRST production period of that sub-period (same convention as the Prediction Table). The sub-period with the highest cut-off automatically covers all remaining cohorts. Example (monthly): 202011, 202111, 202311 produces 3 tables: period 1 starts at 202011, period 2 starts at 202111, period 3 starts at 202311 onward. Works with all date formats (YYYYMM, YYYY, YYYYMMDD, Integer).
chkTruncateCols: Truncate observation columns at cut-off (recommended). Checked: each sub-period Nevada table shows observation columns up to and INCLUDING its own cut-off period (the cut-off date is included as the last column). Unchecked: all sub-periods share the full observation window to the last repair date.
newdatasetNevada: Output dataset name - Nevada table format
newdatasetIC: Output dataset name (Interval-censored) - leave blank to skip
labelDateNote: Select the format that matches EXACTLY how dates appear in each column. All formats are converted internally to YYYYMM for arithmetic. R make.names() changes (X prefix, dots) are handled automatically.

help.title: Build Nevada Table from Shipment and Repair Data
help.body:
Description

Constructs a Nevada (warranty matrix) table from two datasets and optionally also produces the interval-censored output ready for Parametric Survival Analysis (Interval).

Setup
  1. Set the shipment / delivery dataset as the active dataset in BlueSky before opening this dialog.
  2. Select the repair / failure dataset from the dropdown in the left panel. Its columns will then populate the repair column selectors on the right.
Shipment dataset - one row per production cohort:
  • A production month column
  • A delivered / units shipped column (numeric)
Repair dataset - one row per individual repair event:
  • The production month of the repaired unit
  • The calendar month in which the repair occurred
How the Nevada matrix is built
  1. Both production month columns and the repair month column are converted to YYYYMM integers using the declared formats.
  2. Age at repair (months) = repair_month - production_month (both converted to linear month counts).
  3. Repair counts are aggregated by (production month, age).
  4. A full cohort -- age grid is built. Each cohort's maximum observable age = last repair month - cohort production month. Ages beyond this limit are NA (the upper-right triangle).
  5. The grid is pivoted wide and joined to the shipment delivered counts to produce the Nevada matrix.
Supported date formats
  • YYYYMM (e.g. 202501) - six-digit integer
  • MMM-YY (e.g. Jan-25) - three-letter month, 2-digit year
  • MMM-YYYY (e.g. Jan-2025) - three-letter month, 4-digit year
  • YYYY-MM (e.g. 2025-01) - ISO format
  • MM/YYYY (e.g. 01/2025) - month slash year
  • POSIXct (e.g. R date type) - already a proper R date
R make.names() mangling (X prefix prepended to numeric names, dots replacing hyphens/slashes) is reversed automatically - select the original format, not the R-mangled version.

Interval-censored output (optional)
Produces a long-format dataset with Month, Age_L, Age_U, Status. Feed directly into Parametric Survival Analysis (Interval) selecting Age_L as Start time (L) and Age_U as End time (U).
